zeilen.text: I haven't had a whole day off in thirteen years, and the bar hardly ever closes early, because three fishermen would tell the harbour about it by noon. So I've been thinking, just to see what it feels like. If you had me for one whole day with the door locked, where would you take me?
zeilen.gesprochen: I haven't had a whole day off in thirteen years, and the bar hardly ever closes early, because three fishermen would tell the harbour about it by noon. [sigh] So I've been thinking, just to see what it feels like. If you had me for one whole day with the door locked, where would you take me?

zeilen.text: People tell me things all day, and I'm good at it, but tonight I don't want to hear what's wrong with anybody. I don't want to be clever either. Will you just sit here with me and tell me nothing at all?
zeilen.gesprochen: People tell me things all day, and I'm good at it, but tonight I don't want to hear what's wrong with anybody. [sigh] I don't want to be clever either. Will you just sit here with me and tell me nothing at all?

zeilen.text: My father had one rule in his bar for forty years, and it was that everybody drinks: fishermen, mayors and dogs. I've kept it, even on the days when I'd like to throw someone in the harbour. What was the one rule in the house where you grew up, Duc?
zeilen.gesprochen: My father had one rule in his bar for forty years, and it was that everybody drinks: fishermen, mayors and dogs. [chuckle] I've kept it, even on the days when I'd like to throw someone in the harbour. What was the one rule in the house where you grew up, Duc?

zeilen.text: Your cook Lola danced barefoot on my bar again last night, and now my fishermen want to learn. They are all sixty years old, and one of them has a bad hip. Does she do that on your boat too, or does she save it for me?

zeilen.text: Your concierge Sophia sits down at my table and plays me for diesel, and she cheats like a Corsican. I like her very much, and I still win. Do you play cards, Duc, or do you have one of those honest faces?

zeilen.text: My mother rings from Seville once a year, at the end of the season, and she always says the same thing: the bar has had me for thirteen years, and she wants to know when she gets me back. I tell her the line is bad. What does your mother ask you when she rings, Duc?

zeilen.text: My grandmother danced flamenco in Seville with the same pair of castanets for sixty years. I only learned the parts that end on a table. Who in your family can do something that you never could?

zeilen.text: I haven't said a word to the mayor for two years, and in a village this small that takes real work. zeilen.text: You saw Sandru ask me for a grappa that night, the boy from the shop across the street, the one with the new sign on my mother's house. zeilen.text: You were there that morning with my father's photo on the counter, when I told you that I came home from Seville partly because I was scared. You're still the only person who knows that, and I keep waiting to be sorry I said it. Now that you know, is it different when you look at me?

zeilen.text: What I really drink is water, and one coffee at four o'clock when nobody's there, and nobody on my father's board knows that. Lately I've started making two coffees at four, without really deciding to. Will you come and drink the second one, or do I have to pour it away?

zeilen.text: I said it again this morning, to Totò of all people, that everybody's welcome and nobody's mine, and for the first time it felt like a lie. I liked that, and it scared me a little. How long do you want this to stay between you and me, o figliolu?

zeilen.text: I laughed far too loud right after you kissed me, Duc, and that's the laugh I only do when I'm scared. So now you know that you scare me a bit, and I can't take that back. Are you going to do it again?

zeilen.text: I opened my notebook after we were alone the other night, because I write everything down, every meal and every scar, and I sat there for ages. I didn't know which page you go on. Where do I put you, Duc?

zeilen.text: The other night went a lot further than I expected, Duc, and this morning the hen looked at me as if she knew all about it. I talk too much, so I'm going to say this fast, before I start on something else. Can we do that again?

zeilen.text: We slept together, Duc, and then I got up and fed everybody with a very big smile, and one of them bit me and I didn't even care. I stayed in Marseille for a man once, and I was very stupid about it. How do I do this without being stupid again?
